howTo: Choose the Encrypt tab to lock text, or the Decrypt tab to unlock a bundle.
Type or paste your text into the input box.
Enter a strong password and remember it exactly — there is no recovery.
Press the run button and copy the Base64 result.
To decrypt, paste the bundle, enter the same password, and run Decrypt.
keyFacts: AES-256-GCM is authenticated encryption: it detects any tampering with the ciphertext.
Your password is converted to a key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 and 100,000 iterations, a standard slow hash.
A new random 16-byte salt and 12-byte IV are generated for every encryption.
The output is one Base64 bundle: salt + IV + ciphertext, easy to copy or share.
Decryption fails with a wrong password or a modified bundle, by design.

aes-256-gcm-encrypt-decrypt.quickAnswer: This tool encrypts text with AES-256 in GCM mode using your browser's built-in Web Crypto API. Your password is stretched with PBKDF2 (100,000 iterations of SHA-256) into a 256-bit key, and every encryption uses a fresh random salt and IV. Nothing is sent to any server.
aes-256-gcm-encrypt-decrypt.tagline: Military-grade text encryption that runs entirely in your browser.
aes-256-gcm-encrypt-decrypt.workedExample:
Encrypting the text "Meet at noon" with the password "Sunset-42-River":

1. A random 16-byte salt and 12-byte IV are generated.
2. PBKDF2 stretches the password into a 256-bit key.
3. AES-256-GCM encrypts the text and appends a 16-byte authentication tag.
4. You receive a Base64 bundle (about 88 characters) that decrypts back to "Meet at noon" only with the same password.

Note: running it again gives a different bundle, because the salt and IV are fresh each time. Both decrypt to the same text.
